events.title: INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan
events.organiser: Indian National Congress, hosting INDIA bloc parties, with student bodies and civil society organisations
events.place: Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi
events.quote: The Delhi Police has issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) allowing the Congress to hold a one-day rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on November 1, a senior police officer said on Saturday.
events.what: A one-day rally in Delhi organised by the Congress as part of the INDIA bloc's campaign against the SIR. Delhi Police issued a no-objection certificate. Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal said on 24 October that a 'Dilli Chalo March' would end at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November, and Mahila Congress chief Alka Lamba said the rally would not be postponed or cancelled. Rahul Gandhi called it the 'Vote Bachao Desh Bachao Jan March and Maharally' in a post on X on 25 October, and on 31 October gave the march's route from the Connaught Place and Minto Road junction by Ajmeri Gate to Ramlila Maidan, starting at noon. Delhi Traffic Police announced restrictions in central Delhi from 10 am to 5 pm on 1 November. Delhi Police sources told ANI on 31 October that no permission had been sought for a march from Connaught Place. On 1 November senior leaders, among them Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, M. A. Baby, D. Raja and Dipankar Bhattacharya, left Kharge's residence for Minto Road in an open bus to march to Ramlila Maidan, The Hindu reported. The Indian Express reported that Delhi Police put the ground's working capacity at 30,000 to 40,000 people while the organisers expected up to 10 lakh. Rahul Gandhi alleged on X that the BJP had forcibly shut every shop at Connaught Place. The march and rally went ahead on 1 November. The Hindu reported that leaders including Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, M. A. Baby, D. Raja, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Sanjay Raut and Supriya Sule attended, and The Hindu and The Wire report speeches by Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav. Scroll reported that the Chief Ministers of Telangana, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh joined. The Wire reported that the Aam Aadmi Party and the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, which it says are no longer in the INDIA bloc, stayed away, and that the Cockroach Janta Party, which had pledged its support, was absent. Scroll put the crowd at tens of thousands and The Wire at thousands. BJP MP Sambit Patra said about 40% of the ground was empty, and K. C. Venugopal said on X that Delhi had never seen an uprising on this scale, without giving a number. Rahul Gandhi said in his speech that Gyanesh Kumar would be removed as Chief Election Commissioner and would go to jail, and that legal action would follow against Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Kharge said the bloc would keep fighting until Kumar goes. None of the reports read gives a resolution adopted at the rally.

events.title: INDIA bloc 'public impeachment' of the Chief Election Commissioner
events.organiser: INDIA bloc (announced by Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal)
events.place: The lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's official residence, 10 Rajaji Marg, New Delhi
events.quote: The event, originally scheduled for Friday, October 30, will now be held on Saturday, October 31, at the lawns of 10 Rajaji Marg
events.what: A mock Parliament of INDIA bloc MPs and leaders, which the opposition called a 'Jan Mahabhiyog', held on 31 October on the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence after rain put it back by a day. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided and Kharge moved a motion of six charges against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, among them the deletion of 13.2 crore voters through the SIR, the change to Form 6 without Parliament's approval, centralising control of the rolls through the ERONET and ECINET software, and shutting out the other two Election Commissioners. The Hindu reports that the proceedings lasted three and a half hours and that the motion was adopted unanimously by a show of hands. The Wire counted 37 speakers, among them MPs from 18 parties, activists and electors who said their names had been deleted. Rahul Gandhi closed the discussion, called the exercise a 'political weapon' and said Kumar should be removed and tried for treason. It has no legal effect, since a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only by Parliament in the manner of a Supreme Court judge. It came the day before the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November.
